title: Freezing Strawberries To Keep Them Warm? | Frost Protection on the Strawberry Field | Carrigan Farms
description:
Ever wondered why farmers spray WATER on crops when it’s freezing? In this video, we’re out in the fields at Carrigan Farms in Mooresville, NC, battling a late-season frost to save our 2026 strawberry crop. We’re using a process called latent heat of fusion. By continuously watering the strawberry plants, the water releases a tiny amount of heat as it turns to ice, keeping our delicate strawberry blossoms at a safe 32 degrees, even when the air temperature drops much lower. If we don’t do this, we lose the flowers. and that means no strawberries for picking season!

In this video, you’ll see:
- The overhead irrigation system in action across the strawberry patch 
- What the "ice-encased" blossoms look after frost protecting 
- Why this method is the secret to a successful harvest after blooming
